findings.detail: The changelog introduces a separately funded daily floor that pays providers a top-up when closed-UTC-day inference earnings fall below 110% of a seven-day baseline. The baseline is frozen at first opt-in and includes sponsored inference. It adds admin funding and baseline-repair endpoints, persistent consent evidence and per-machine receipts across identity aliases. This is a new money-moving surface on the payment ledger (A-009) and a new incentive for a malicious provider (ADV-001). A provider could inflate the frozen baseline with self-routed or sponsored traffic, or exploit alias or machine identity handling, to extract top-ups. The canonical model has no TB-008 or threat entry for floor payments, baseline integrity, double-payment across aliases, or admin-endpoint misuse. The changelog also says existing accounting archives do not cover the new financial tables. Fix: add a threat entry and mitigations for baseline manipulation, canonical-machine deduplication, the cumulative pool cap and admin authorization. Confirm that sponsored or self-consumed traffic is handled, and keep payments disabled until that review is done. The code was not supplied, so this finding rests on the changelog description only.
